text:
Priya: Idea: instead of full VPC peering or static NAT pools per customer, what if we implement ephemeral egress leases? Agent in customer VPC requests a lease for a few seconds/minutes that pins a tenant to a specific egress IP+port range on our regional gateway. This would let customers maintain a stable outward socket while avoiding permanent peering. Thoughts?
Ethan: Sounds like SNAT port preservation but managed at the connection level. How do leases map to TCP/UDP flows and to HTTP keepalive?
Priya: Lease metadata includes src_vpc_cidr, tenant_id, port_range, ttl, and a binding token. Agent programs local iptables to SNAT to local port-range and inserts the binding token into requests (X-Redwood-Egress-Lease). Gateway verifies lease and maps the source port to the tenant's allowlist IP.
Rhea: Concern: NAT exhaustion on the regional gateway if many leases with large port ranges. Need a packing algorithm and backpressure. Also per-tenant fair-share for ports.
Gavin: We can implement a small allocator: each lease gets a min-port-count (e.g., 16 ports) default, adjustable by SLA. Gateway maintains ephemeral allocation map + LRU reclamation when TTL expires.
Ethan: What about UDP/random ephemeral ports (we serve embeddings over UDP-like protocols)? Lease should support UDP but require shorter TTLs and active keepalives.
Priya: Agreed. For UDP we require client keepalive heartbeat every N seconds or lease auto-expiry.
Rhea: Security: how do we prevent port-poaching or forged leases? Bind leases to agent identity via mTLS and require signature on lease requests. Gateway verifies signature and rejects mismatched origins.
Priya: Workflows: 1) Agent authenticates to controlplane -> requests lease for tenant T, desired ports P, ttl. 2) Controlplane allocates ports from regional pool and signs lease. 3) Agent programs local SNAT and provides binding token to app layer OR kernel-level NAT uses mapping automatically. 4) Gateway maps incoming packets from that ephemeral port range to tenant allowlist IP.
Gavin: Failure modes: agent offline -> lease expires -> connections break. Need graceful degradation: fallback to shared NAT (loses stable IP), and app should tolerate reconnects. Emit metric lease_loss_count.
Ethan: Implementation detail: do we want the agent to do the SNAT or for the gateway to rewrite based on header token? Agent-side SNAT reduces gateway state but requires kernel changes and more permissive routing. Header-based rewrite preserves agent simplicity but is vulnerable to header spoofing unless TLS terminates at gateway.
Rhea: For Private (on-prem) installs we can run the egress-gateway inside customer network (virtual appliance) so agent only requests local lease and gateway does the real egress mapping. For hosted, gateway runs in our region and agent must use mutual TLS to request leases.
Priya: Port allocation strategy: use per-region port bitmap shards, keep small contiguous chunks for latency-sensitive flows. For very high throughput customers allow larger contiguous ranges via dedicated reserved blocks.
Gavin: Observability: metrics per-tenant: leases_active, ports_allocated, lease_renewals, lease_reclaims, lease_conflicts. Add logs with minimal PII: tenant_id, region, port_range, lease_id.
Ethan: Data plane scaling: gateway needs efficient packet rewrite on high throughput (millions conn/sec). We should implement lease mapping in an AF_XDP or eBPF path to avoid slow userland. Also have a fallback kernel NAT path for lower scale.
Rhea: Legal/compliance: storing tenant->port mapping is sensitive; retention policy must be short and encrypted. Add option for customers to opt out of ephemeral mapping logs.
Priya: Rollout plan: PoC in staging with single region, basic allocator + eBPF mapping, small customer canary (2 tenants). Evaluate port-churn and connection failure patterns.
Gavin: Product questions: which customers get this? Likely dedicated/private customers wanting stable source sockets but who can't or don't want peering. Could be opt-in via console with quota.
Ethan: Edge cases: long-lived TCP tunnels (SSH) — recommend persistent leases with stricter auth and longer TTL or fallback to peering. Also need to handle VIP failover across regional gateways (rebind leases on failover).
Priya: API sketch for lease request:
POST /v1/egress/leases
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <agent-token>
Body: {"tenant":"acme","ports":32,"proto":"tcp","ttl":120} -> returns {"lease_id":"l-xyz","port_range":"61000-61031","gateway_ip":"3.120.45.8","signed_lease":"..."}
Gavin: Ops: include a lease garbage collector, watcher to reclaim ports when leaks detected, and a leak-alert when port_utilization > 80% for more than 5m.
Rhea: Threat model: replayed signed_lease must be prevented by binding to agent cert + src IP + nonce. Include monotonic lease counters for revocation.
Ethan: Migration: for customers currently using per-customer NAT pools, offer a migration tool to migrate allowlists to the ephemeral gateway IP + port ranges, or keep a small reserved static block for compatibility.
ops-bot: task created: https://internal/tasks/EGRESS-LEASES-POC to track PoC steps and add to infra board.
Priya: I'll start a design doc with capacity sims and allocator heuristics. Demo target: 3-week PoC.
Gavin: Add me for the eBPF path design.
Rhea: I'll write the compliance/retention checks and opt-out UI text.
Priya: Thanks team. Keeping this opt-in seems safest. :rocket:
